sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看到其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于 nytimes.com 免费直播精选采访，供任何人观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: As Ukraine's president implores the United States Congress to intervene in the war, I spoke with my colleague, David Sanger, about the potential paths forward in the war
sentences.zh: 随着乌克兰总统恳请美国国会干预这场战争，我与我的同事大卫·桑格探讨了这场战争潜在的发展方向

sentences.en: and which of them is most likely to occur.
sentences.zh: 以及其中哪一种最有可能发生。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, March 17th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月17日，星期四。

sentences.en: David, we want to talk to you about the paths forward in Ukraine, what happens next in this war.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我们想和你聊聊乌克兰未来的走向，这场战争接下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: And the president of Ukraine, Volodymyr Zelensky, just proposed one such path forward in a speech to Congress, and I want you to describe it.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基刚刚在国会演讲中提出了这样一个发展方向，我想请你描述一下。

sentences.en: Well, the scene in front of Congress, Michael, was really quite remarkable.
sentences.zh: 好的，迈克尔，国会大厦前的场景确实相当引人注目。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Madam Speaker, members of the Congress, ladies and gentlemen.
sentences.zh: 众议院议长女士，国会议员们，女士们先生们。

sentences.en: As you would imagine, President Zelensky showed up in what is now his uniform, which is his Churchill in a T-shirt look, right,
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，泽连斯基总统穿着他现在标志性的服装出场，也就是他的“丘吉尔穿T恤”造型，对吧，

sentences.en: where he is clearly calling in from an embattled presidential office at a moment that his capital is under siege.
sentences.zh: 很明显，他是从一个四面楚歌的总统办公室进行连线，当时他的首都正处于围困之中。

sentences.en: Right now, the destiny of our country is being decided.
sentences.zh: 此刻，我们国家的命运正面临抉择。

sentences.en: The destiny of our people, whether Ukrainians will be free.
sentences.zh: 我们人民的命运，以及乌克兰人能否获得自由。

sentences.en: He immediately invoked images that he knew would resonate with his audience,
sentences.zh: 他立刻唤起了他深知能引发共鸣的画面，

sentences.en: Democrats and Republicans.
sentences.zh: 民主党人和共和党人。

sentences.en: Remember September the 11th, a terrible day in 2001, when evil tried to turn your cities, independent territories, in battlefields, when innocent people were attacked.
sentences.zh: 请记住9月11日，2001年糟糕的一天，当邪恶企图把你们的城市、独立的领土变成战场，当无辜的人民遭到袭击。

sentences.en: And the unspoken message of that was that just as the world rallied with the United States and the U.S.
sentences.zh: 其潜台词是，正如当时世界与美国站在一起、美国

sentences.en: rallied with the West then, you must do it now.
sentences.zh: 与西方站在一起一样，你们现在也必须这样做。

sentences.en: Russia has turned the Ukrainian sky into a source of death.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯已将乌克兰的天空变成了死亡之源。

sentences.en: And then he made a requeSt.
sentences.zh: 随后他提出了一个请求。

sentences.en: To create a no-fly zone over Ukraine to save people.
sentences.zh: 在乌克兰上空建立禁飞区以拯救人民。

sentences.en: Is this too much to ask?
sentences.zh: 这要求过分吗？

sentences.en: A couple of times in the speech, for a no-fly zone.
sentences.zh: 他在演讲中多次提到建立禁飞区。

sentences.en: I have a dream.
sentences.zh: 我有一个梦想。

sentences.en: These words are known to each of you.
sentences.zh: 这些话你们每个人都很熟悉。

sentences.en: Today I can say, I have a need.
sentences.zh: 今天我可以这样说：我有一种需求。

sentences.en: I need to protect our sky.
sentences.zh: 我需要保护我们的天空。

sentences.en: But it was an ask that...
sentences.zh: 但这是一个……的请求

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Slava Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰荣耀。

sentences.en: Even as he received the warmest, most unanimous applause from Congress you've heard in recent times, everyone in the room, including Zelensky himself,
sentences.zh: 尽管他受到了国会近年来最热烈、最一致的掌声，在场的每个人，包括泽连斯基自己，

sentences.en: knew he wasn't going to get it.
sentences.zh: 都知道他不会得到这个。

sentences.en: Well, explain that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，解释一下。

sentences.en: How exactly a no-fly zone works and why it's not an option.
sentences.zh: 禁飞区究竟是如何运作的，为什么它不是一个选项。

sentences.en: You know, no-fly zones sound so passive.
sentences.zh: 你知道，禁飞区听起来很被动。

sentences.en: It's as if you lay out on Google Maps an area where no aircraft are allowed.
sentences.zh: 就好像你在谷歌地图上画出一个不允许任何飞机进入的区域。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The way downtown Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 正如华盛顿特区市中心

sentences.en: is known to be a no-fly zone for commercial aircraft and private aircraft.
sentences.zh: 对商业飞机和私人飞机来说是已知的禁飞区一样。

sentences.en: But the fact of the matter is that to enforce a no-fly zone, you have to do two things.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，要强制执行禁飞区，你必须做两件事。

sentences.en: You have to patrol its perimeter and be willing to shoot down any plane that is coming in to violate that zone.
sentences.zh: 你必须在其周边巡逻，并准备击落任何试图飞入并违反该区域的飞机。

sentences.en: And the second thing you have to be ready to do is to take out the anti-aircraft batteries down on the ground that might shoot up at planes defending the no-fly zone.
sentences.zh: 你必须准备做的第二件事是，摧毁地面上可能向保卫禁飞区的飞机开火的防空炮台。

sentences.en: And in the case of Ukraine, the Russian anti-aircraft batteries are in Russia.
sentences.zh: 就乌克兰而言，俄罗斯的防空炮台位于俄罗斯境内。

sentences.en: So there would be no way to enforce that no-fly zone without conducting a military attack on Russian bases and Russian territory.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果不发对俄罗斯基地和俄罗斯领土的军事攻击，根本无法强制执行这个禁飞区。

sentences.en: And that is, as President Biden has said multiple times now, the road to World War III.
sentences.zh: 正如拜登总统多次说过的那样，这是通往第三次世界大战的道路。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So given that this is not going to be the path forward, a no-fly zone enforced by the U.S.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这不会是未来的前进道路——由美国及其盟友在乌克兰强制执行禁飞区，我们想和你探讨这场战争在未来几天、几周甚至几个月内可能如何发展的其他潜在方向。

sentences.en: and its allies in Ukraine, we want to talk through with you the other possible paths forward for how this war may play out in the coming days, weeks, maybe months.
sentences.zh: 我们根据你的报道以及我们同事的报道，提出了四种方案。

sentences.en: And we've come up with four scenarios based on your reporting and the reporting of our colleagues.
sentences.zh: 第一种方案是这场战争能否通过外交手段走向结束。

sentences.en: The first scenario is whether this war can be brought to a conclusion through diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 在过去几天里，俄罗斯和乌克兰官员一直在会面，试图达成外交解决方案。

sentences.en: For the past few days, Russian and Ukrainian officials have been meeting to try to achieve a diplomatic solution.
sentences.zh: 以色列、德国和法国等国的领导人似乎每隔一天就会与普京通电话，试图寻找外交解决途径。

sentences.en: The leaders of countries like Israel, Germany, and France get on the phone with Putin, it seems, every other day to try to find a diplomatic solution.
sentences.zh: 这场冲突的外交结局会是什么样子的？

sentences.en: What might a diplomatic end to this conflict look like?
sentences.zh: 那么，我根据我交谈过的人，为你勾勒一下外交结局的一些可能方案。

sentences.en: So let me paint a scenario for you about some of the possibilities for a diplomatic end from people I've talked to.
sentences.zh: 首先，俄罗斯对乌克兰和泽连斯基总统提出了一系列三项要求，尽管普京总统承诺他会结束战争，

sentences.en: First, the Russians have a set of three demands for Ukraine and for President Zelensky, even though President Putin's commitment that he would end the war,
sentences.zh: 即使泽连斯基总统同意这些要求，也并非完全明确。

sentences.en: even if President Zelensky agreed to these demands, is not entirely clear.
sentences.zh: 但俄罗斯表示乌克兰需要同意以下几点。

sentences.en: But here's what the Russians have said Ukraine would need to agree to.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们必须放弃对克里米亚的任何主权宣称——俄罗斯在2014年入侵并随后吞并的领土。

sentences.en: The first is they would have to give up any claim to Crimea, the territory that Russia invaded in 2014, and then annexed.
sentences.zh: 第二个要求是，乌克兰东部两个自行宣布独立的共和国，

sentences.en: The second demand is that the two eastern self-declared republics of Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 顿涅茨克和卢甘斯克，过去八年来一直在那里进行着残酷的战争，必须被乌克兰承认完全独立的国家。

sentences.en: Donetsk and Luhansk, where there's been this grinding war being fought for the past eight years, would have to be recognized as completely independent states by Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 第三个要求是，乌克兰必须公开宣布其中立地位，可能类似于奥地利这样的国家，

sentences.en: And then the third is that Ukraine would have to publicly declare its neutrality, probably along the lines of a country like Austria,
sentences.zh: 它拥有军队，但没有太大的军事能力。

sentences.en: which has a military but not much military capability.
sentences.zh: 他们必须声明将不再寻求加入北约，尽管这目前已经写进了乌克兰宪法。

sentences.en: And they would have to say that they would never again seek to join NATO, even though that's written right now into the Ukrainian constitution.
sentences.zh: 所以宪法必须进行修改。

sentences.en: So the constitution would have to be amended.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我们认为泽连斯基会对这些要求持开放态度吗？

sentences.en: And David, do we think that Zelensky might be open to those demands?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他已经表示他愿意讨论其中至少一部分要求。

sentences.en: Well, he's indicated that he's open to discussing at least some of them.
sentences.zh: 例如，他说他已经不再指望北约会随时让乌克兰加入西方联盟。

sentences.en: For example, he has said that he's moved beyond the hope that NATO was going to let Ukraine into the Western alliance anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象他可能愿意接受中立，但要放弃克里米亚和那两个东部共和国，天哪，那可差得太远了，

sentences.en: So you could imagine how he might be willing to accept neutrality, but giving up Crimea and those two eastern republics, boy, that's a much further reach,
sentences.zh: 因为这基本上等于把他的国家大约三分之一的领土割让给俄罗斯。

sentences.en: because he would essentially be ceding to Russia roughly a third of his country.
sentences.zh: 所以大卫，我们假设有一刻泽连斯基确实同意了俄罗斯的几项条款。

sentences.en: So David, let's assume for a moment that Zelensky does agree to several of these Russian terMs.
sentences.zh: 我想俄罗斯可能仍然需要某种保证，即美国和欧洲实施的这些严厉制裁将得到放松，

sentences.en: I imagine Russia might still need some kind of assurance that these crippling sanctions that have been imposed by the United States and Europe will be relaxed
sentences.zh: 作为任何外交解决方案的一部分。

sentences.en: as part of any diplomatic solution.
sentences.zh: 嗯，完全正确。

sentences.en: Well, that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人会坚持解除这些严厉的制裁，这些制裁很可能在未来几天内导致他们债务违约，并将卢布跌至历史最低水平，

sentences.en: The Russians would insist that these crippling sanctions, which are likely to send them into default in coming days and have plunged the ruble to its lowest levels
sentences.zh: 并真正开始对普通俄罗斯人造成影响，他们需要得到保证这些制裁将被解除。

sentences.en: and really begun to bite on ordinary Russians, they would need an assurance that those would get lifted.
sentences.zh: 因此有趣的是，周二晚上，国务卿布林肯在接受美国国家公共电台（NPR）采访时表示，要开始解除制裁，

sentences.en: So it was interesting that on Tuesday night, in an interview with NPR, Secretary of State Lincoln said that for the sanctions to begin to lift,
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯必须完全且不可逆转地撤出乌克兰，也就是说，必须有某种保证机制，

sentences.en: the Russians would have to withdraw completely from Ukraine and irreversibly, that is to say, there would have to be some method of assurance
sentences.zh: 确保在未来两、三年或五年内，俄罗斯不会卷土重来、重蹈覆辙。

sentences.en: that in the next two or three or five years, the Russians couldn't just turn around and go back and do this all over again.
sentences.zh: 所以你突然发现，虽然这是一场俄罗斯和乌克兰之间的谈判，但此时此刻其中还有许多其他参与者。

sentences.en: And so now you're suddenly discovering that while this is a negotiation between Russia and Ukraine, there are a lot of other players in it at this moment.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，这场危机的外交解决方案非常棘手。

sentences.en: So, in short, a diplomatic solution to this is very tricky.
sentences.zh: 非常棘手，但最终是必要的。

sentences.en: Very tricky, but ultimately necessary.
sentences.zh: 很难想象这场战争在没有某种外交解决方案的情况下结束。

sentences.en: It's hard to imagine this war ending without some kind of diplomatic solution.
sentences.zh: 好吧，大卫，我们来谈谈第二个潜在的发展方向。

sentences.en: Okay, David, let's turn to the second potential path forward.
sentences.zh: 假设目前没有外交解决方案。

sentences.en: Let's say there is no diplomatic solution for now.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰和俄罗斯无法达成一致。

sentences.en: Ukraine and Russia can't get on the same page.
sentences.zh: 感觉几乎按定义来说，这随后就会变成一场漫长而残酷的消耗战，持续更多周，甚至更多月。

sentences.en: It feels like, almost by definition, this then becomes a long grinding war of attrition that lasts many more weeks, maybe many more months.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们来讨论这种可能性。

sentences.en: So, let's talk through that possibility.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，恐怕我要说这很有可能发生。

sentences.en: Well, Michael, I'm afraid to say that's a very strong likelihood.
sentences.zh: 你所看到的是持续不断的狂轰滥炸。

sentences.en: What you've seen is constant bombardment.
sentences.zh: 这表明普京相信，只要他继续战斗，并不惜任何人员代价（甚至直接针对平民）夺取更多领土，

sentences.en: And that suggests that Putin believes that if he just keeps battling on and can grab some more territory at whatever human cost, even with civilians targeted directly,
sentences.zh: 无论何时外交取得成果，他都将处于更有利的谈判地位。

sentences.en: that he would be in a better negotiating position whenever that diplomacy comes to fruition.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这将以成千上万甚至数万人的生命为代价。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, that would come at the cost of thousands, if not tens of thousands of lives.
sentences.zh: 但这似乎并没有困扰

sentences.en: But that does not seem to be bothering
sentences.zh: 普京总统或目前的俄军。

sentences.en: President Putin or the Russian forces right now.
sentences.zh: 唯一可能阻碍这一点的是，普京本人正在承受非常惨重的损失。

sentences.en: The only thing that might get in the way there is that Putin himself is taking very big losses.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 关于这些损失有多大存在争议，但五角大楼上周表示，已有数千名俄罗斯士兵阵亡或以某种方式伤亡。

sentences.en: There are disputes about how big those losses are, but the Pentagon said last week that thousands of Russian troops have been killed or were casualties in some way.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实向你表明他承受着一定的压力，因为迟早人们会发现他们在俄军服役的儿子和女儿死在了

sentences.en: So, it does suggest to you that he's under some pressure because sooner or later, people are going to discover that their sons and daughters in the Russian military died
sentences.zh: 一场俄罗斯总统仅形容为“特别军事行动”的战争途中。

sentences.en: on the way into a war that the president of Russia only described as a special military action.
sentences.zh: 我们的理解是，普京愿意这样做吗？愿意承受对他自己军队的损失，并摧毁大部分乌克兰——按他自己的说法，

sentences.en: And is it our understanding that Putin would be willing to do that, incur the losses to his own army and destroy much of Ukraine, which by his own account
sentences.zh: 乌克兰是俄罗斯的延伸，是他由于钟爱而想要重新拉回俄罗斯势力范围的地方。

sentences.en: is an extension of Russia, and the place he wants to draw back into the Russian sphere because it's beloved.
sentences.zh: 那么，他为什么还要毁掉它呢？

sentences.en: So, why would he want to destroy it?
sentences.zh: 这是关于普京内心想法的一个核心谜团，即他对乌克兰人的看法是如何变得强硬的。

sentences.en: This is a central mystery about what's going on in Putin's mind of how he's hardened in his view about the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 但是，迈克尔，他为了夺取这片领土并实现他的梦想会走多远，这个问题对于当前在美国以及北约盟国中

sentences.en: But, you know, Michael, the question of how far he would go in order to seize this territory and realize his dream is so central to the argument taking place now
sentences.zh: 进行的争论来说至关重要。

sentences.en: in the United States and among the NATO allies.
sentences.zh: 周三早些时候，总统国家安全顾问杰克·沙利文与他的俄罗斯同行通了电话。

sentences.en: Earlier on Wednesday, there was a phone call between Jake Sullivan, the president's national security advisor, and his Russian equivalent.
sentences.zh: 这次通话是自这场战争爆发三周以来，我们所知的白宫与克里姆林宫之间的首次接触。

sentences.en: And that phone call is the first contact that we're aware of between the White House and the Kremlin in the three weeks that this war has gone on.
sentences.zh: 沙利文先生做了什么？

sentences.en: And what did Mr. Sullivan do?
sentences.zh: 他花了很大一部分时间警告俄罗斯人，如果他们在乌克兰对乌克兰人民使用化学或生物武器，将会产生什么后果。

sentences.en: He spent a good deal of it warning the Russians about the consequences that would flow if they used chemical or biological weapons in Ukraine against the Ukrainian people.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 大卫，在你概述的这种情况下，

sentences.en: David, in this scenario you're outlining,
